responsibility: `rustc_hir` defines and organizes the compiler’s High-level Intermediate Representation and the crate-local metadata needed to identify, classify, traverse, and persist it. Its crate root (`lib.rs`) ties the crate together by wiring modules, re-exporting the main HIR-facing APIs, and declaring the arena integration, while `arena.rs` specifies which HIR and related payload types are arena-allocated. The core HIR data model lives in `hir.rs`, which defines HIR nodes, items, expressions, patterns, types, embedded identifiers, and helper APIs; `hir_id.rs` provides the stable local identity system for those nodes via `OwnerId`, `HirId`, and `ItemLocalId` and conversions to definition identifiers. For traversing and querying HIR, `intravisit.rs` supplies the standard visitor framework and default walking logic, and `pat_util.rs` adds focused utilities for analyzing pattern structure and bindings. To connect HIR to name resolution and definition identity, `def.rs` defines the central classification and resolution types such as `DefKind` and `Res`, `definitions.rs` maintains the crate-local table of definitions, hierarchical def-path information, `LocalDefId` assignment, and stable `DefPathHash` computation, and `def_path_hash_map.rs` provides the specialized hash-table mapping from local def-path hashes to `DefIndex` values. The crate also records special compiler-known items: `lang_items.rs` defines the language-item catalog, metadata, storage, and lookup routines; `weak_lang_items.rs` identifies the weak subset of language items and their linker symbols; `diagnostic_items.rs` stores the mapping between diagnostic item names and `DefId`s. For attribute and semantic classification, `target.rs` categorizes HIR items into attribute-checking targets. For persistence and incremental compilation, `stable_hash_impls.rs` defines the stable hashing context and hashing implementations that make HIR identifiers and crate-level HIR data hash reproducibly. Error reporting support in `errors.rs` provides HIR-specific wrapper errors such as missing lang-item failures. Finally, `tests.rs` validates stable properties of the definition-path hashing infrastructure. Together, these pieces make `rustc_hir` the compiler crate that owns the HIR representation itself plus the stable identities, definition metadata, traversal APIs, special-item registries, and hashing support required for later compiler phases to analyze Rust programs consistently.
